requirements.R1: Own the product area end-to-end: get clear on the problem, write requirements people understand, rally the team to ship
requirements.R2: Build the roadmap around what's true, not what's loudest — data, client feedback, market signals
requirements.R3: Partner closely with Engineering and Design
requirements.R4: Let the numbers tell you if it worked — track metrics, talk to real users, iterate
requirements.R5: Say the hard thing clearly; make tradeoffs visible; help the team make good calls fast
requirements.R6: Demonstrated success shipping products with ownership of complex cross-functional initiatives
requirements.R7: A bias to ship — no endless debate
requirements.R8: Technical fluency to discuss architecture and engineering tradeoffs
requirements.R9: A real belief in financial inclusion
requirements.R10: Systems thinking and ability to simplify complex problems
requirements.R11: Comfort working with ambiguous, messy data
requirements.R13: Scrappy, happy to wear different hats
requirements.R15: Collaborative, empathetic leadership with diverse stakeholders

questions.q: What has Jordanne owned end to end, and where did she take something from problem definition all the way to shipped?
How does Jordanne decide what goes on a roadmap when the loudest stakeholder wants something the data doesn't support?
How does Jordanne work with engineers and designers day to day?
How does Jordanne know whether something she shipped actually worked?
Tell me about a time Jordanne told leadership something they didn't want to hear.
What is the most complex cross-functional initiative Jordanne has shipped, and who did she have to bring along?
Does Jordanne ship fast or deliberate for a long time? Give me evidence either way.
How technical is Jordanne really? Can she hold her own on architecture and engineering tradeoffs?
Does Jordanne care about financial inclusion or expanding access to financial services?
What does systems thinking actually mean in Jordanne's work? Show me it rather than telling me.
How does Jordanne handle a problem where the data is messy, incomplete or contradictory?
Walk me through how Jordanne breaks down a problem she has never seen before.
Is Jordanne scrappy? Has she done the unglamorous work herself rather than delegating it?
How does Jordanne explain something technical to an executive who doesn't have the background?
What is Jordanne like as a leader when stakeholders disagree with each other?
What does Jordanne know about the economics of a points-based loyalty program — earn rates, burn, liability, margin?
Which ecommerce surfaces has Jordanne personally owned and operated?
What payment methods and checkout work has Jordanne shipped?
Has Jordanne launched a subscription product, and how did it perform?
Has Jordanne owned acquisition and retention together, or only one side?
How has Jordanne handled peak trading events and systems under heavy load?
What experience does Jordanne have designing cash-back rewards?
